reviews.review: As if Borderlands and Doom had a child.

It was a really fun game at first. My friends and I would play a lot just messing around and having a good time. But after these last few major updates the game is just not fun anymore.
From replacing the perks and how they work all the way to the limits of what you can do in-game whether it be single player or with your friends.

Even though I have many personal problems of why me and my friends don’t like playing this game anymore as stated there personal and are not really a problem for the game. Just something I personally think the Devs change to force players to slow down in-game which adds more playtime. aka more playtime does not equal fun or enjoyable.

What is a real problem is mainly two things that me and my friends not only agree upon when talking about it, but keep unironically and unintentionally bringing up when playing.

1. Perks(the blue,red,yellow,and orange perks) are now combo items instead of being just a single piece. With you now only being able to carry three. Sure each perk item has unique abilities with them but it makes you have to stop and waste time on what you want to pick, slowing you down and adding wasted time in-game ruining the run. This is especially the case in multiplayer as mentioned

2. Limits and barriers to multiplayer and even single player, recently the Devs made it so that you and your friends can no longer upgrade each other's weapons after you upgrade them yourself. I know it can make you overpowered but trust me when I say the weapons that are even on par with levels in-game feel under-powered. And what's even the point of playing with friends if you can’t mess around and have fun. Even if that means doing OP or meta game type stuff.

Overall it feels like the game has become a grind just to even have a little fun. With each update and change to the game there are more things to slow you down or force limits upon you which can ruin a good or enjoyable session singleplayer or multiplayer. 

TLDR; Forcing limits and changing in-game mechanics to slow you down or add unnecessary obstacles do not make a fun game for both single and multiplayer.
reviews.developer_response:
Hey!

We're sorry to hear that after 40 hours of gameplay, our changes made you enjoy the game less than before.

We'd love to know more and potentially address the issues you're mentioning. Though, we'd also like to let you know how we perceive the changes you're talking about, in the hope that you might see why they were needed.

1) 'Limiting what you can do in the game, both in Single or Multiplayer'
We're unsure to understand that part of your analysis and we'd love to better understand it.

2) 'Changes made to slow-down the game' & 'We have to waste time choosing what item to choose'
If anything, we'd like to promote fast-forward combat and we're trying our best to incentivize it. The in-game timer is paused most of the time when choosing rewards and we'll also modify the weapon drop system to make them drop when the ingame timer is paused as well (which is not the case currently). When it comes to choosing perks in multiplayer, you can always wait until you're in a safe zone or a time-paused situation to pick them. We're unsure of what other mechanics you think are slowing the game, but this is not what we'd like to do. We might have under estimated the impact of some of our changes and if so, we'd love to hear more about it.

3) 'Removing the level-up weapon console'
We understand that you loved mini-maximizing your runs by exchanging your weapons with your brobot and power-leveling them. We removed it to incentivize players at switching weapons more often. Though, to be fair, using that trick only increased the damage you dealt by 5%, is that enough to consider that it was "necessary" in order to be on-par with enemies of that level, we're not sure. We understand if you feel that way but we think it's not the case.

In any case, we're really sorry to hear that after liking the game for as much as 40 hours, you now dislike it. We can only hope that our future updates and changes will make you like it even more than you did before.

Have a good day!

reviews.review:
It does not matter how good a game is if it has not got the fundamental parts needed in a game then there is no point the graphics are nice and colorful smooth game play and responsive controls lots of mods thats the good.
One game i should not have bought if you are like me im in my 5o's now and my reactions are not what they used to be and NO SAVE what a waste of a game each time you die you start again at base came and have to do it all again.
reviews.developer_response:
Hey there.

We're sorry to hear that the Roguelite format (starting again when dying) feels like a waste of time to you.

However, there are plenty of upgrades you can unlock in between two runs which can make your subsequent runs easier and help you progress further into the game each time you retry.

As for the 'missing' fundamental parts, we'd love to hear what you think is missing.

Roboquest as an Early Access game has still a lot of room to grow and we're always trying to polish and refine what's already there while adding what we deem is missing to the game.

In the hope that we'll manage to add what you think is missing and that you'll enjoy playing our game, have a great day!

reviews.review:
Do you like rogue-lite FPS time-trial Doom-athons that offer nearly endless replayability with a friend? Hectic frenzies of bullets, lasers, and... robots? Classes that are vastly different? RPG-lite customization?

Do you want devs who update quickly? Respond to community feedback and change the game based on it? Have a clear vision for their game?

Pick this one. Buy it now. Stop reading. No really. Right now.

This game is great value for money. Instead of buying one new Square Enix game, just buy this game 5 times! It'll go to a group of devs that are producing something magic, and your friends will owe you for introducing them to something that's so much fun.
